The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-4,3].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. Given that $f(3)=2,$ what is the minimum value ${f}_{\text{min}}$ of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-4,3]?$

question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the maximum value of $f(x)$ on $[-4,3]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval. 

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-4,3),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=-2.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-4,-2,3.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

The function is made up of $2$ triangles. Let's add the areas bounded by these shapes to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14205687/assets/c30d7e1d2c9eb939726d85b0ee5d51a2bdc0cfe73fab92f0ba29839a9f18be4e.png)

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & =2 \\ f(-2) & =f(3)+{\int }_{3}^{-2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =f(3)-{\int }_{-2}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2-7.5 \\  & =-5.5 \\ f(-4) & =f(3)+{\int }_{3}^{-4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =f(3)-{\int }_{-4}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2-(-3+7.5) \\  & =2-4.5 \\  & =-2.5\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates. 

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{2,-5.5,-2.5\}=-5.5.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-5.5,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=-2.$
